newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes firmer following Dutch sale.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes firmer following Dutch sale.

text.p: Gold prices advanced on Monday morning following an announcement from the Dutch Central bank that it has sold 300 tonnes of gold from its reserves.
Rumours of a sale from a central bank of around 10 million ounces (300 tonnes) had been current in the market for weeks and were a key factor behind gold's loss of value late last year.
The announcement came after the gold price had bounced off 3-1/4 year lows struck last week after gold's downtrend began to accelerate from the beginning of the year.
Gold fixed at $359.60 per ounce following $358.25 on Friday afternoon, to build on minor firmness in New York late on Friday and in Tokyo and Hong Kong earlier today.
"The (Dutch) news is probably bullish short term and bearish long term," said bullion analyst Andy Smith of Union Bank of Switzerland. "People are probably buying the volatility."

The bank said the bullion sales, representing more than 20 percent of its total holdings, had brought the share of gold in its total holdings of gold and foreign exchange into line with with that of other gold-holding countries.
Transactions would be settled in February and March this year and be reflected in the bank's summary balance sheet.
The Dutch central bank also sold some 20 percent of its then gold reserves in November-December 1992 totalling 276 tonnes.
Before the Dutch announcement, dealers said business had been quiet in Europe. Immediately after the news, the reaction largely involved the professionals so far.
Prices were forecast to consolidate as charts registered oversold signals and the markets showed signs of steadying.
"The charts are all showing heavy indications of being oversold. It's more likely that we will have a series of consolidation moves rather than see it (gold) go roaring back up," one dealer said.
The extent of gold's change in sentiment was explained by a dealer who said that the market was now willing to buy on dips rather than concentrate on selling any up ticks.
"It looks like $362-$364 could be the limit for now. But there are still some people calling for $330," a dealer said.
The other precious metals were easier. Silver was a cent lower at $4.75/$4.77 platinum was $1.25 down at $363.25/$364.25 and $122.25/#1223.25 off $0.75. --Brian Spoors +44 171 542 8058
